[[File:Aronia Blossoms Screen 2.jpg|right|thumb|500px|''Hanami Blossoms Screen'' by {{ill|Kanō Naganobu|es|Kanō Naganobu|ja|狩野長信|qid=Q11571493|lt=Kanō Naganobu}} (狩野長信), depicting Furyū Odori during the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|ar|فترة أزوتشي-موموياما|ast|Periodu Azuchi-Momoyama|be|Перыяд Адзуці-Мамаяма|bg|Адзучи-Момояма|br|Marevezh Azuchi-Momoyama|ca|Període Azuchi-Momoyama|ckb|سەردەمی ئازوچی-مۆمۆیاما|cs|Období Azuči-Momojama|de|Azuchi-Momoyama-Zeit|eo|Azuĉi-Momojama-epoko|es|Período Azuchi-Momoyama|eu|Azuchi-Momoyama aroa|fa|دوره آزوچی-مومویاما|fi|Azuchi-Momoyama-kausi|fr|Époque Azuchi Momoyama|he|תקופת אזוצ'י-מומויאמה|hu|Azucsi–Momojama-kor|id|Zaman Azuchi–Momoyama|it|Periodo Azuchi-Momoyama|ja|安土桃山時代|ka|აძუტი-მომოიამა|ko|아즈치모모야마 시대|lt|Momojama laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Azuchi–Momoyama|nl|Azuchi-Momoyamaperiode|no|Azuchi-Momoyama-perioden|pl|Azuchi-Momoyama|pt|Período Azuchi-Momoyama|ro|Perioada Azuchi-Momoyama|ru|Период Адзути-Момояма|simple|Azuchi–Momoyama period|sk|Obdobie Azuči-Momojama|sr|Азучи-Момојама период|sv|Azuchi|th|ยุคอาซูจิ–โมโมยามะ|tl|Panahong Azuchi–Momoyama|tr|Azuchi-Momoyama Dönemi|uk|Період Адзуті-Момояма|vi|Thời kỳ Azuchi-Momoyama|wuu|安土桃山时代|zh|安土桃山时代|zh_min_nan|Azuti-Momoyama sî-tāi|zh_yue|安土桃山時代|qid=Q319531|lt=Azuchi–Momoyama period}}.]]
'''Furyū Odori''' (風流踊) or simply '''Furyū''' (風流) is a type of [[Japanese traditional performing arts|medieval Japanese performing art]] featuring groups of performers dancing in elaborate costumes or disguises to the accompaniment of instruments like [[:en:Gongs|Gongs]] (鉦), {{ill|Drums|de|Drums|it|Drums|qid=Q3715553|lt=Drums}} (太鼓), and flutes, as well as singing or chanting.<ref name="nishi">Nishikado (2004)</ref> It was especially popular during the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}. 

This art form embodied the aesthetics of elaboration and beauty, capturing the attention of audiences with its visual appeal.

== Overview ==

Furyū Odori involves performers dressing in colorful or {{ill|Costume|af|Kostuums|ar|زي|az|Kostyum|bg|Носия|bn|কস্টিউম|br|Gwiskamant|da|Kostume|el|Ενδυμασία|eo|Kostumo|es|Disfraz|et|Kostüüm|eu|Janzkera|fa|کاستوم|fr|Costume|fy|Kostúm|gd|Aodach-brèige|he|תחפושת|hi|वेशभूषा|hr|Kostim|hy|Տարազ|id|Kostum|it|Costume (abito)|ja|衣装|jv|Kostum|kk|Костюм|ko|코스튬|la|Ornatus|lt|Kostiumas|mk|Костум|nl|Kostuum|no|Drakt|nr|Ivunulo|pt|Traje|ru|Костюм|sd|پوشاڪ|sh|Kostim|simple|Costume|sv|Dräkt|ta|ஆடை|tr|Kostüm|uk|Костюм|ur|ملبوسات|zh_yue|服裝|qid=Q9053464|lt=disguised}} attire, dancing to the rhythms of gongs, drums, and flutes.<ref name="nishi"/> Over time, the term ''furyū'' expanded to include not only the dances but also the processions of splendid [[Matsuri float|Floats]] (山車) and the dances performed around them. This performance art has roots in [[Yōgō ritual dances|rituals against plagues]], [[Nembutsu chanting|Buddhist chanting]], and {{ill|Dengaku|ca|Dengaku|es|Dengaku (música)|fa|دنگاکو|fr|Dengaku|id|Dengaku|it|Dengaku|ja|田楽|ko|덴가쿠 (춤)|pl|Dengaku|ru|Дэнгаку|qid=Q3022455|lt=ritual agricultural performances}}.<ref name="nishi"/> 

Following the turbulent {{ill|Ōnin War|ar|حرب أونين|azb|اونین ساواشی|bg|Онинова война|ca|Guerra Ōnin|cs|Válka Ónin|de|Ōnin-Krieg|es|Guerra de Ōnin|et|Ōnini sõda|eu|Ōnineko gerra|fa|جنگ اونین|fi|Ōnin-sota|fr|Guerre d'Ōnin|hu|Ónin-háború|id|Perang Ōnin|it|Guerra Ōnin|ja|応仁の乱|ka|ონინის წლების ომი|ko|오닌의 난|lt|Onino karas|ms|Perang Ōnin|nl|Onin-oorlog|pl|Wojna Ōnin|pt|Guerra de Ōnin|ru|Война годов Онин|simple|Ōnin War|sr|Онински рат|sv|Oninkriget|th|สงครามโอนิง|tr|Ōnin Savaşı|uk|Смута Онін|vi|Chiến tranh Ōnin|wuu|应仁之乱|zh|应仁之乱|qid=Q385676|lt=Ōnin War}} (1467–1477), Furyū Odori gained momentum, spreading widely as a performance art centered around dancing. A historically significant example is the depiction of Furyū Odori in the ''[[Toyokuni Festival Screen]]'' during the {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} (1603–1868), the emphasis on ephemeral aesthetics diminished, and Furyū Odori transformed into fixed rural traditions.<ref>Sasaki (2003), pp. 238–251</ref> Many dances were incorporated into agricultural rituals like {{ill|Rainmaking|en|Rainmaking|qid=Q7284934|lt=Rainmaking}} and became favored by the ruling {{ill|Samurai|en|Samurai|qid=Q38142|lt=Samurai}} class. Despite many Furyū Odori traditions disappearing, some, such as those in {{ill|Iga Province|en|Iga Province|qid=Q1047128|lt=Iga Province}} ({{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}), have been preserved.<ref>Sasaki (2003), pp. 238–251</ref>

Furyū Odori served as the precursor to numerous [[folk performing arts]] and [[:en:Festivals|Festivals]], including [[Nembutsu Odori]], [[:en:Bon Odori|Bon Odori]], [[:en:rain dances|rain dances]], and [[insect warding rituals]]. Other derivatives include [[Taiko drum dancing]], [[:en:kenbu|kenbu]] (sword dancing), and Buddhist-inspired [[Hotoke-no-mai]].<ref name="nishi"/><ref group="note">Eastern Japan's lion dances and [[deer dances]] (鹿踊) also trace their origins to Furyū Odori. Nishikado (2004)</ref>

In February 2020, the [[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] recommended Furyū Odori as a candidate for the {{ill|Intangible cultural heritage|en|Intangible cultural heritage|qid=Q84036549|lt=Intangible cultural heritage}} list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/92050401.html|title=Proposal for UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Registration|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs|date=2020-02-19|accessdate=2020-02-19}}</ref> By November 30, 2022, Furyū Odori was officially recognized as part of the list, encompassing 41 events across 24 prefectures.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASQCZ457RQCYUCVL02Z.html|title=Furyū Odori Added to UNESCO List|newspaper=Asahi Shimbun Digital|date=2022-pp-30|accessdate=2022-pp-30}}</ref> Despite this recognition, Japan's total number of intangible cultural heritage registrations remained at 22, as this was a collective registration.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/2022pp01/k00/00m/040/037000c|title=Furyū Odori Recognized by UNESCO|newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun|date=2022-pp-01|accessdate=2022-pp-30}}</ref>
